issues.body: gated_test_modules() detects an inline `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "x"))]`, or a plain `#[cfg(test)]` only when a path component's parent `mod name;` declaration is feature-gated. It does not associate a local stacked `#[cfg(feature = "x")]` with a following `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }`, a normal equivalent Rust spelling. Such a module can be added under an otherwise ungated source file and this gating check will still return no gap, contradicting the claimed guarantee that every feature-gated lib-test module has a CI executor. The current non-vacuity tests exercise only lane parsing, not this detector false-negative.
issues.fix_hint: Parse adjacent cfg attributes on test-module declarations (including the stacked `cfg(feature)` plus `cfg(test)` form), and add a synthetic source-tree test proving that this spelling is reported uncovered without a matching `--lib` lane and covered with one. Either support the broader cfg forms claimed by the test or narrow the documented invariant explicitly and enforce the repository's permitted spelling separately.
issues.title: Detector misses locally feature-gated plain test modules

verdict.summary: The CI command changes are sensible and the new Python test passes, but the structural gate is incomplete for a common Rust cfg spelling and can therefore report success while feature-gated lib tests remain unexecuted. Its stated invariant is broader than what its detector enforces.
